ov: A large monkey of west-central African rainforests and one of the most colourful mammals, with red and blue skin on its face and rump. It is the most sexually dimorphic primate: males are far bigger than females, with longer canines and brighter colours.
len: Males 70–95 cm, females 55–70 cm (head and body)
rg: Southern Cameroon, mainland Equatorial Guinea, Gabon and parts of the Republic of the Congo.
df: Mostly fruit and seeds, plus leaves, mushrooms and animals from insects to young duikers.
fx: Mandrills live in "hordes" that can number in the hundreds; hordes in one Gabon park averaged 620 animals.
Adult males live alone and rejoin the horde only in the breeding season.
